children: British retail spending grew modestly in October despite higher petrol prices and households cutting back on some categories of spending in anticipation of Black Friday deals, according to a survey published on Tuesday.
The British Retail Consortium said spending in shops increased by 1.5% in annual terms in October, above September's 1.3% growth and the strongest rise since June.

"With consumers facing higher household costs, caution ahead of the Budget, and some waiting for Black Friday deals, overall sales growth was modest," said Linda Ellett, UK head of consumer, retail and leisure at accountants KPMG, who sponsor the BRC survey.

However, a separate survey from Barclays, based on consumer card spending data on a wider range of goods and services, showed the strongest growth since July 2025 with a 2.3% annual increase last month, up from September's 2.0% rise.
The BRC's measure of food sales was up by 3.2% while non-food sales were flat
BRC CEO Helen Dickinson said cupboard staples rose modestly after the British government advised households to stock up for emergencies
Barclays' gauge of consumer confidence showed the least optimism about the UK economy since April
Growth in Barclays' measure of essential spending rose by 3.1%, driven by a 22.7% increase in fuel spending, while spending on non-essentials was up by 1.9%
Entertainment had its strongest month since September 2024 after tickets went on sale for the Glastonbury music festival
The BRC survey covered the four weeks to October 31
The Barclays spending data covered card spending between September 25 and October 10 while the consumer confidence data was based on polling between October 23 and October 27
